article.description: — Kyrie Irving scored 25 points and Cooper Flagg had 22 points, eight rebounds and six assists as the Dallas Mavericks used a late 11-0 run to beat the Los Angeles Clippers 110-100 on Saturday night.

article.story: DALLAS -- — Kyrie Irving scored 25 points and Cooper Flagg had 22 points, eight rebounds and six assists as the Dallas Mavericks used a late 11-0 run to beat the Los Angeles Clippers 110-100 on Saturday night. Walter Clayton Jr. added 16 points and Max Christie finished with 13, both off the bench, as Dallas (9-7) began a back-to-back with a second consecutive win at home following an 0-3 trip. Brook Lopez scored 17 of his 21 points in the second half to lead the Clippers (4-11), who have dropped three straight overall and are 0-7 on the road. Rui Hachimura had 19 points, matching a season high with four 3-pointers. After the Clippers’ Kris Dunn hit a corner 3 that cut Dallas’ lead to 91-88 with 5:12 left, the Mavericks scored 11 in a row aided by two Los Angeles turnovers. Irving opened shooting 1 of 7 from the floor but scored 12 points in the fourth quarter. Flagg went 7 of 13 at the foul line, the first time last season’s NBA Rookie of the Year — an 84.2% free-throw shooter — has missed six in his brief career. Clayton and Christie combined to go 5 of 7 from behind the arc. The Clippers entered last in the NBA in rebounding, averaging 39 per game. They beat the Mavericks on the boards 54-52 but were outscored 20-19 in second-chance points. The Mavericks played their first game this season without starting forward P.J. Washington Jr., who sat out with an illness. Up next Clippers: Visit Houston on Monday. Mavericks: At Utah on Sunday night to begin a three-game trip. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here
